title: Beer locker at a university-district convenience store, late night
moment: At 11:30 pm a student buys a six-pack from an unattended self-service alcohol locker outside a 24-hour convenience store near NTU. Today the kiosk asks them to scan the front of their National ID card or driver's licence so a back-office service can read the birth date, and the image is stored with the sale log for 'compliance'.
verifier: Operator of the self-service alcohol locker (convenience-store franchisee / vending operator)
predicate: Holder's age on today's date is at least 18 (threshold on birth date), proven without revealing birth date, ID number or name
disclosed_today: Full ID image or scan: name, ID number, birth date, photo, household-registration address, kept in the transaction log
issuer: Ministry of the Interior household registration system, via the TW FidO / digital ID wallet
why_zk: Strong fit: the machine only needs a yes/no on age >= 18, yet it retains a full identity record, creating a breach target with no staff to apply judgment. Weakness: the operator's liability may make it want proof an adult was present for each sale, so a bare proof may not satisfy a regulator that expects a log; a per-sale proof receipt (no identity) would have to be accepted as that log.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: In HIPAA Safe Harbor, a checklist of enumerated identifiers is removed before sharing and the holder must still judge leftovers; here, the age-threshold proof plays the removal step by guaranteeing the log contains none of the ID's enumerated fields, so no leftover judgment is needed.

In PDPA Art. 11(3), data must be deleted when its purpose lapses but an open 'needed for our duties' exception lets the collector keep it; here, a proof that never contains the birth date plays the role of making retention exceptions moot because nothing identifying exists to retain.

title: E-cigarette vending kiosk in a night-market station concourse
moment: A 20-year-old at an MRT station concourse wants to buy nicotine-free vape pods from a vending kiosk. Because the Tobacco Hazards Prevention Act restricts e-cigarette-type products and sales to minors, the kiosk requires an ID photo plus a selfie, which are sent to a vendor cloud for matching and stored.
verifier: Kiosk vendor and its cloud age-verification subcontractor
predicate: Holder is at least 18 (or the statutory minimum for the product) as of today, proven with a credential bound to the holder's device, with no face image sent
disclosed_today: ID card photo, selfie biometric, name, birth date, ID number, transmitted to a third-party vendor
issuer: Ministry of the Interior (household registration), as holder of the authoritative birth date
why_zk: Good fit: the unattended kiosk sends biometric and ID data to a subcontractor, so two parties see the full identity. The vendor then learns who bought what. Using a threshold proof, the subcontractor role disappears. Weakness: binding the proof to the person at the machine (rather than a borrowed phone) still needs a device unlock or liveness step, and that step is not solved by the credential alone.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: In Tor onion routing, relays are layered so no single intermediary holds both origin identity and destination; here, the age proof plays that role by letting the kiosk see 'adult yes' and purchase while the cloud vendor never sees identity, so no party holds both who and what.

In HIPAA minimum necessary, the holder is told to release only what the purpose needs but has no mechanism proving minimality; here, the threshold proof plays the mechanism, making the released subset provably just 'age >= 18'.

title: Hotel-lobby minibar and craft-liquor vending machine for foreign visitors and residents
moment: A resident foreigner with an ARC, and a Taiwanese guest, each try to buy a bottle from a lobby vending machine at a tourist hotel in Hualien. Today the hotel front desk photocopies the passport or ARC to unlock the machine for the room, and the copies sit in a folder.
verifier: Hotel operator running an alcohol vending machine unlocked via the front-desk system
predicate: Holder is over the legal drinking age, proven from either a Taiwan ID or ARC credential, without disclosing nationality, passport number or ARC number
disclosed_today: Photocopy of passport or ARC (name, nationality, document number, birth date, photo) retained by the hotel
issuer: National Immigration Agency for ARC holders, Ministry of the Interior for citizens
why_zk: Moderate fit: the hotel already collects passport copies for registration, so the vending step adds little new exposure for guests already checked in. Value is mainly for non-guests and for ending an extra retained copy. Weakness: foreign tourists without any Taiwan-issued credential cannot use this, and their home-country ID would need a separate issuer, so coverage is partial.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: In the household-register proxy-copy ruling, an office may collect ID copies at its own discretion with no stated limit; here, the hotel's discretionary photocopying plays that role, and the threshold credential replaces discretion with a fixed single-predicate answer.

In HIPAA Safe Harbor, identifiers of relatives and employers are stripped alongside the individual's own; here, the proof omits nationality and document number the way Safe Harbor drops secondary identifiers, so only the age fact is shared.
